subject: arithmetic errors with policy a la Boost

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: arithmetic errors with policy a la Boost
parts:
Eureka!

Having just read the Boost math lib approach to
errors, I think we'd be well served to follow their
very sensible lead:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_47_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/main_overview/error_handling.html

The basic ideas are:

* a taxonomy of different kinds of errors (domain error,
overflow, rounding, pole, etc.)

* four different actions on error (set error number,
throw exception, ignore, user-defined)

* each pair of error-type and behavior results determines
an action and return value

* final template parameter for error-handling policy that's
set to a statically determined default controllable by macro

It'll also have two nice properties: (a) our error handling
will be compatible with Boost's, and (b) we'll inherit the
documentation.

Along with this, we'll want to follow C++'s arithmetic and
the std lib's lead in returning NaN values where appropriate.
In most cases, we'll get this behavior for free propagated
through our results. For instance, if we have a negative
variance and take its square root, we'll get a NaN which will
propagate to the result.

This is all based on the policy pattern, which is also used in Eigen
for arithmetic (it's what we're overriding to allow auto-dif
variables to integrate into Eigen).

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_47_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/policy/pol_overview.html

We already discussed using a template parameter with a default.

We're already using Boost's metaprogramming templates for
result type calculations:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_47_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/main_overview/result_type.html


so we're already compatible there.

The one issue I didn't see the answer to is whether to check
all arguments, even if some are unused. This'll come up when
we override the log probability functions to only compute
up to a proportion. Some constants aren't actually used, but
may be out of range.

It's a lot of work to do all this the right way, but I
think it'll turn out to be easier in the long run in terms
of saving on doc and consistency and compatibility. On that
note, I leave you with:

http://xkcd.com/974/

- Bob
